SITE STRUCTURE — five doors

/            Home
/team        Team dashboard, rebuilt nightly
/players     Player database — Red Wings / In the system
/players/…   Player page, with the data portrait
/articles    One feed, filtered by subject, newest first
/articles/…  Article page
/glossary    Every number defined, with a worked example
/about

No news/analysis split: nothing here expires on a news cycle. Subject tags do the sorting, and the featured slot is curation rather than a category — it stands only while the feed is unfiltered.

The trade tree and the redraft are internal tools, not site features. They can be SUBJECTS of an article; nothing embeds.

System: greyscale interface, Doto for page titles, Space Grotesk for reading, IBM Plex Mono for anything numeric. Wings red appears ONLY inside a data visualisation.
Working: switch between Red Wings and In the system, filter by position, sort any column. The Articles index filters by subject too. Everything else is a static mockup.

THE SYSTEM TAB IS BLOCKED ON DATA, NOT DESIGN.

NHL API /v1/prospects/DET returns empty, and where it does return players it carries bio only — no league, no club, no stats. No public expected-goals model covers the AHL, CHL, NCAA or Europe, so that table can never show xG or percentiles the way the roster table does.

Rather than invent numbers, the tab ships the real column set, ghost rows for density, and a panel naming the three candidate sources and what each costs you.

DATA PORTRAIT, replacing the headshot: one solid dot per goal scored, one hollow dot per expected goal. Unique to each player, generated from the pipeline, no image rights. DeBrincat reads 41 solid against 37 hollow.

THE ARTICLE TEMPLATE CARRIES THE ARGUMENT, NOT JUST THE NUMBER.

The Copp piece now runs past the gap into where it came from: a dumbbell chart of expected against actual shooting percentage, then three findings that point in different directions — the sample is tiny, two teammates missed the same way, and a residue that might be real — closing on a stated verdict and a panel naming what would actually settle it.

Every figure in it is computed from data/site/skaters.json. Copp: 115 shots, 9 goals, 7.8% actual against 17.2% expected — the highest expected rate on the roster.
